newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 27.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
CHANGE OF GOVERNOR IN UTTAR PRADESH RULED OUT

The Uttar Pradesh governor protested over the home minister's recent that the the law and order situation was deteriorating in the state. The state administration's move was seen as a rebuttal to the home minister's observation in parliament that the state was heading for anarchy. However, the home minister ruled out any immediate change of governor in Uttar Pradesh, saying the government would not intervene directly in the state.
The Hindustan Times
SPEAKER ABOLISHES MEMBERS' QUOTA FOR PHONES AND GAS

The speaker of the lower house directed the government to abolish the quotas earmarked for members of parliament (MPs) relating to allotment of telephone and cooking-gas connections. The scrapping of the quota would become effective from April 1, 1997. The speaker's announcement was welcomed by a majority of MPs, who had often pleaded in the house for the withdrawal of the quota given to them for such allotments.
The Economic Times
12 PCT RAILWAY FREIGHT HIKE PROPOSED

The railway minister presented an inflationary budget which was bound to have a cascading effect across several industries. The railways proposed to mobilise an additional 18 billion rupees in 1997/98 (April-March) with a 12 percent across-the-board hike in freight rates. Upper class passenger fares were also hiked by 5-10 percent. Although the railways calculated the impact of the proposed hike on the wholesale price index as a meagre 0.127 percent, its ripple effect, especially on industrial inputs, would be much higher.
SCHEME TO TAP UNACCOUNTED OVERSEAS DEPOSITS

The government would float a foreign currency-denominated India Amnesty Infrastructure Development Bond scheme to tap the vast unaccounted overseas bank deposits maintained by resident Indians. This was the first time that the government was considering offering an amnesty scheme for undisclosed wealth parked outside the country. The scheme was expected to pump in close to $5 billion into the infrastructure sector in the first year.
INTERNATIONAL AIR CARGO SECTOR OPENED TO PRIVATE OPERATORS

The Director General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) announced new guidelines for private operators to undertake international cargo operations. This brought the monopoly of Lufthansa, KLM and Air-India in cargo operations to an end. To date, only international carriers have been allowed to operate international cargo operations. The DGCA also issued guidelines to allow domestic cargo airlines to operate international services from all five international airports and some other domestic airports in the country.
Financial Express
UNIT TRUST SHORTLISTS CONSULTANTS

The state-owned financial institution Unit Trust of India (UTI) shortlisted four international consultants for its proposed foray in the insurance sector. The final winner for the consultancy contract out of Price Waterhouse, Coopers & Lybrand, McKinsey & Co and KPMG Peat Marwik was expected to be announced in the UTI board meeting scheduled next Monday. UTI's plan for entering the insurance sector depended on the extent the government would finally allow private firms to compete with the two state-owned insurance corporations.
INDUSTRY DEMANDS MAY NOT BE MET: JAMES CAPEL

The budget will not fulfil most of industry's key demands, James Capel B&K, the broking-cum-research arm of the HSBC group, felt. A survey carried out by James Capel said industry associations and corporates provided the former with certain reasonable demands which the industry would like to be addressed in the budget. However, based on its own research, James Capel did not expect several of these sectors' demands to be met.
Business Standard
FIVE PCT HIKE IN 1997/98 OUTLAY LIKELY

The plan outlay for 1997/98 (April-March) would be around 910 billion rupees, a less than five percent increase over the current year's plan size of 870.86 billion rupees, Finance Ministry sources said. The annual plan size was kept low on account of the ministry's reluctance to enhance budgetary support, expected to be around 38 percent of the plan size. The government was also trying for savings in the plan by asking ministries to go slow on expenditure until March.
STEPS TO OPEN UP INSURANCE SECTOR EXPECTED

The Finance Minister is expected to seek parliamentary approval to formally set up the insurance watchdog when he presents his budget for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March). Spurred by growing international clamour and the need to speed free-market reforms launched in 1991, the country has taken several steps to lure investment in insurance, but stopped short of actually letting foreigners in.
The Observer
COMMODITY FIRMS TO BE HIT HARD

The bottom lines of commodity companies would come under severe pressure following the freight hike announced in the railway budget. The hike would push up input costs by way of inward freight increases of raw material and an expected upward revision in power tariff. However, sluggish market conditions and increasing competition from cheap imports would not allow these companies to pass on the increased input costs to the customer.
CEMENT, STEEL SCRIPS HAMMERED

Cement and steel stocks were subjected to heavy bear hammering in major bourses following the hike in freight charges in the railway Budget. Scrip prices of most cement and steel manufacturing majors closed below the previous's close. Other stocks also drifted in a lacklustre trade on the Bombay bourse (BSE), dealers said. The BSE top 30-share index ended 9.67 points higher at 3,366.5 in a day of range-bound trade.
Business Line
GLOBAL PLAYERS SHOULD SET UP ASSEMBLY PLANTS

The consumer electronic and television manufacturers' association (CETMA) asked the government to ensure global players, entering the Indian market, set up full-fledged assembly plants. This would ensure greater commitment to India, the industry body said. CETMA said the entry of multinationals subjected domestic companies to unfair competition in a 58 billion rupee, stagnated market.
